description: standards/032-secrets.md SE5: how a secret is recognised at the log and error boundary. Recognition is by declaration, never by pattern: at start the emitter is given the value of every secret the service declares (secret-declaration.schema.json) and replaces any occurrence of one, in any string field at any depth, with the declared marker naming the declaration. A closed list of field names is redacted by name as well, because an inbound Authorization header or a caller's password is a secret the service did not declare and could not have. Shape matching - a regex for a key prefix, an entropy threshold - is admitted only as a third, best-effort layer and is never the mechanism, because a declared secret with an unremarkable shape is still a secret; corpus.json's redaction detector is exactly that case.

declared_values.match: substring, case-sensitive, in every string at every depth of the emitted object, longest declared value first

connection_string: the userinfo password component, where the URL carries one

fields.match: field name compared case-insensitively after replacing '-' with '_'; the whole value is replaced whatever its type
